headline_draft: OpenAI Ships GPT-Live: Native Voice Model with Sub-300ms Latency
summary: On September 13, OpenAI launched GPT-Live, a native voice AI model powering ChatGPT Voice with sub-300ms latency and emotional nuance. The release eliminates the text-pipeline bottleneck that plagued previous voice implementations, where speech was converted to text, processed, and converted back to audio. GPT-Live processes voice end-to-end, enabling more natural, lower-latency voice experiences. The model also retains emotional context in responses, making interactions feel more conversational.
why_pm: For PMs building voice-first products, GPT-Live's sub-300ms latency redefines the experience ceiling. Latency under 500ms is the perceptual threshold for natural conversation; this crosses it. The emotional nuance also matters: if your product is customer-facing (support, onboarding, coaching), voice now carries tone, not just words. This shifts voice from a 'nice-to-have' to a core interaction pattern you need to design around.
key_facts: Native voice model replaces text-pipeline architecture
Sub-300ms latency (below perceptual threshold for natural conversation)
Emotional nuance retained in audio responses

headline_draft: Visa, Mastercard, Ant International align on Know-Your-Agent standard for AI shoppers
summary: Visa, Mastercard, and Ant International announced the Know-Your-Agent (KYA) interoperability framework on September 12, 2026, unifying three previously competing protocols: Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol, Mastercard Verifiable Intent, and Ant's Agentic Mobile Protocol. The framework allows card networks, wallets, agent platforms, and marketplaces to recognize trusted AI shoppers across ecosystems. This represents the first major industry alignment on agent identity and trustworthiness standards, directly addressing the friction of agents acting on behalf of users in payment and commerce workflows.
why_pm: If you're building commerce, fintech, or multi-agent products, this standard simplifies cross-platform agent deployment and reduces compliance friction. PMs shipping AI-powered shopping experiences now have a clear interop layer to reference when pitching to payment partners and enterprises.
key_facts: Know-Your-Agent (KYA) framework unifies Visa, Mastercard, and Ant protocols
Enables agents to be recognized as trusted across card networks and wallets
Aligns three competing standards into single interoperability layer
Applies to card networks, wallets, agent platforms, and marketplaces
quotes: Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol, Mastercard Verifiable Intent and Ant's Agentic Mobile Protocol — so card networks, wallets, agent platforms and marketplaces can recognize trusted AI shoppers across ecosystems
